title: Train sprint synthesis and hotfix roster
summary: Sprint wrap-up notes for the Mar 3 release train. Contains hotfix roster, canary observations, short change log for the train, risk items to watch, and prioritized action items ahead of the next train.
notes: Meeting: Release Engineering weekly sync — sprint synthesis
Attendees: Aisha (owner), Daniel, Sofia, Liam, Priya, Marcus, plus on-call SRE (Elena Rodriguez joined for rollouts)
Objective: Consolidate learnings from last release train, confirm hotfix rostering and rollback readiness, and surface triage for outstanding infra flakiness affecting packaging jobs.

Context: This train pushed v1.7.2 (hosted/dedicated runtime improvements + quantization fixes). Two post-deploy incidents (one partial canary degradation, one packaging timeout) were observed — both contained but require follow-ups. We are preparing a small hotfix window for Friday 2025-03-07 for a speed-critical rollback/patch if needed.

Result: No emergency rollback required; canary remained majority-green after automatic fallback but we identified a regression in long-sequence batching that increases tail latency ~12% on p95 for certain configs. Packaging CI flakiness traced to intermittent NFS timeouts on release-builder-3 during heavy parallel builds.
hotfix_roster: Primary: Daniel Kim — pager 24/7 (hotfix owner for Fri window)
Secondary: Sofia Martinez — assist with rollback scripts and canary redeploy
SRE on-call: Elena Rodriguez — infra and routing adjustments
Build lead: Marcus Chen — packaging build triage
QA liaison: Priya Singh — smoke test approvals and gating
change_log: - reduced attention memory copy for quantized kernels (PR #842)
- fallback policy: automatic degrade path to v1.7.1-compat for models with > 8k context
- telemetry: added batching latency histogram tags
- release-builder autoscaling adjusted to avoid packing more than 12 concurrent heavy builds on a single NFS mount
- canary routing: enable circuit-breaker at 10% error budget per instance
observations: Canary incident: at 02:15 UTC canary for model-gamma reported sustained 6% error rate for 10 minutes on a subset of 5 instances. Automatic fallback kicked in, shifting traffic to v1.7.1-compat. Root cause suspected: ordering of KV cache eviction in combined batching path.

Packaging CI: median build time jumped from 18m to 37m for builds that hit release-builder-3. Logs indicate occasional NFS stalls ~120s. Marcus will propose mitigation (local tmpfs ephemeral staging) in follow-up PR.

Telemetry: the new batching histogram exposed hot spots — top contributing factor to p95 tail is a 2x slower kernel selection on a minority of GPU types (older driver versions). Needs driver-policy alignment with infra images.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: If long-sequence batching regression persists clients with >4k context may see higher p95 latency. Mitigation: rollback knob to force legacy batching behavior; prioritize fix in next minor release.

Risk: Packaging CI stalls could delay future trains. Mitigation: short-term — route heavy builds to builder pool excluding release-builder-3; medium-term — implement tmpfs staging and NFS timeouts tuning.
Risk: Canary false positives when telemetry sampling is low. Mitigation: increase sampling rate for first 30 minutes post-deploy for models with >1000 QPS.
action_items: Daniel: Prepare hotfix runbook and smoke test checklist for Fri 2025-03-07 (due 2025-03-05)
Marcus: Draft PR to add tmpfs staging and NFS timeout tuning on builder nodes (target PR by 2025-03-06)
Sofia: Write short doc on fallback policies and add explicit feature-flag for legacy batching (due 2025-03-10)
Priya: Compose end-to-end smoke test matrix for canary vs fallback paths and own gating for hotfix window (due 2025-03-06)
Elena: Coordinate with infra to pin GPU driver versions on canary pool to match supported kernels (check by 2025-03-08)
Aisha: Summarize this meeting and post to #release-engineering with links to PRs and JIRA tickets (done)
All: Review runbook and confirm availability for Fri hotfix window (reply in thread by 2025-03-04)
Follow-up meeting: Quick pre-hotfix sync on 2025-03-07 08:00 PT — 20 minutes
metrics_snapshot: Canary error budget: 1000 requests/min allocated; incident consumed ~65 requests over 10 minutes
Packaging CI median build time: 18m -> 37m for affected runs
Release success rate (deploys that passed all smoke gates): 92% this quarter
decisions: Do hotfix window Friday 2025-03-07 if p95 tail remains above 220ms for the affected jobs after mitigation steps
Enable temporary routing override to reduce canary traffic for model-gamma to 10% until legacy batching flag is available
Exclude release-builder-3 from heavy parallel builds until tmpfs mitigation is merged
next_meeting: Pre-hotfix sync: 2025-03-07 08:00 PT (20m). Weekly release engineering sync: 2025-03-10 10:30 PT
postmortem_plan: If a hotfix or rollback occurs, owner (Daniel) will file a short incident report within 24 hours to confluence and link the postmortem to JIRA RED-2564. Include timeline, impact, root cause, corrective actions, and retro notes.
notes_to_self: Capture a brief checklist for future trains: 1) pre-deploy driver-image alignment, 2) NFS timeout alarms on builders, 3) canary extended-sampling for 30m, 4) verified rollback knob documented in runbook.
